desc: Updated July 2026: how NYSHIP and the Empire Plan typically cover detox, residential, PHP, IOP and MAT for NY employees. Verify free. Call 631-800-4691.
h1: NYSHIP Rehab Coverage in 2026: What Your Plan Helps Pay For
bodyHtml:
Updated August 2026. Federal parity protections and New York's behavioral-health coverage rules remain in force for the 2026 plan year, so NYSHIP and the Empire Plan continue to cover medically necessary addiction treatment. Because plan details can change each year, the surest way to know your current benefits is a free verification.

If you or a loved one is a New York State or government employee, your NYSHIP coverage — most often through the Empire Plan — typically includes meaningful benefits for addiction treatment. Coverage varies by your specific plan and the level of care you need, but in most cases your behavioral-health benefits extend across the full continuum of substance-use treatment. This page explains, in plain language, what is generally covered and how to put those benefits to use. If you are unsure where to start, your employer’s Employee Assistance Program (EAP) can provide a confidential assessment and help coordinate the referral process before treatment begins.

What NYSHIP Typically Covers for Addiction Treatment

The Empire Plan and most NYSHIP options are built to cover medically necessary care across several levels. While exact benefits, prior-authorization rules, and your share of the cost depend on your plan, the following levels of care are commonly covered when clinically indicated.

Medical Detox

Medically supervised withdrawal management for alcohol, opioids, or benzodiazepines is typically covered when it is medically necessary. Learn more about detox coverage.

Residential / Inpatient

Round-the-clock residential rehab may be covered when a lower level of care would not be safe or effective. See residential treatment.

PHP & IOP

Partial hospitalization and intensive outpatient programs are commonly covered and often fit around a work schedule. See outpatient options.

MAT

Medication-assisted treatment, such as buprenorphine or naltrexone, may be covered under medical or pharmacy benefits. Read about MAT.

How Parity Law Protects Your Behavioral-Health Benefits

The federal Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA) requires that most health plans cover mental-health and substance-use treatment on terms no more restrictive than they apply to medical and surgical care. In practice, that means your plan generally cannot impose harsher visit limits, higher cost-sharing, or tougher authorization hurdles on addiction treatment than it does on comparable physical-health care.

Parity does not guarantee that every service is covered or that there are no rules at all — plans can still require that care be medically necessary and, for some services, pre-authorized. But it does give you a strong, defensible basis to expect real coverage for addiction treatment. Your records are also protected: federal rules under 42 CFR Part 2 and HIPAA keep substance-use treatment information confidential.

Understanding Your Share of the Cost

We never quote exact dollar amounts, because they vary by plan and by year. What we can do is explain the factors that shape your out-of-pocket cost so there are no surprises:

  • Deductible: the amount you may pay before the plan begins paying its share.
  • Copay or coinsurance: your portion of each covered service.
  • In-network vs. out-of-network: using participating providers typically lowers your cost.
  • Prior authorization: some levels of care must be approved in advance for benefits to apply.
  • Out-of-pocket maximum: a yearly cap that, once reached, can limit further cost-sharing.

How to Use Your NYSHIP Benefits

Using your coverage does not have to be complicated. A typical path looks like this:

  • Verify benefits. Confirm what your specific plan covers and any authorization requirements. We offer free, confidential coverage verification.
  • Get an assessment. A clinical evaluation, often guided by ASAM criteria, identifies the appropriate level of care.
  • Obtain authorization. When required, we help coordinate prior authorization with your plan.
  • Begin treatment. Care can range from detox to residential to outpatient, stepping down as you stabilize.

Job protection may also be available. The Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) can provide eligible employees with job-protected leave for treatment, and many state employees have additional leave protections.

Employee Assistance Programs and State Wellness Resources

In addition to your NYSHIP behavioral health benefits, New York State employees may have access to Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs) through their agency. EAPs typically provide free, confidential short-term counseling, referrals to community treatment resources, and guidance for employees and family members navigating substance use challenges. According to SAMHSA’s workplace behavioral health resources, EAPs are an important complement to formal treatment — particularly during the transition back to work after a residential stay.

Key things to know about EAPs and addiction treatment: EAP counselors can conduct an initial substance use assessment and provide short-term support, but most EAP plans limit sessions (commonly 3–6). For moderate to severe addiction, EAPs work best as a bridge — connecting you to your NYSHIP benefits for longer-term care rather than serving as your primary treatment. Some agencies also offer state wellness programs that may include peer support specialists and recovery coaching independent of your EAP allotment. Contact your agency HR office or Employee Assistance provider to confirm what is available alongside your NYSHIP coverage.

Get Clear Answers, Free and Confidential

You do not have to decode your benefits alone. Our team can review your NYSHIP or Empire Plan coverage, explain your options, and outline next steps — at no cost and with your privacy protected. To see exactly what your plan covers, visit does NYSHIP cover rehab or call us. This page is informational and not medical advice; clinical decisions should be made with a qualified provider.

Call 631-800-4691 or email support@alumniaidservices.com to get started.

title: NYSHIP Detox Coverage in 2026 | Alcohol, Opioids & Benzos
desc: Updated for 2026: how NYSHIP and the Empire Plan typically cover medically supervised detox for alcohol, opioids and benzodiazepines. Call 631-800-4691.
h1: Does NYSHIP Cover Medically Supervised Detox in 2026?
bodyHtml:
Updated August 2026. Medically supervised detox remains a covered, medically necessary benefit under NYSHIP and the Empire Plan for the 2026 plan year. Specific copays and authorization steps can vary by plan and year, so verify your current benefits before you start.

Detox is often the first step in recovery, and for many substances it is also a matter of safety. If you are a New York State or government employee, your NYSHIP coverage — usually the Empire Plan — typically covers medically supervised detox when it is medically necessary. Coverage varies by your specific plan, but withdrawal management is a core part of addiction care that parity law is designed to protect.

What Is Medically Supervised Detox?

Medically supervised detox, or withdrawal management, is care that helps your body clear a substance safely while clinicians monitor your symptoms and manage them with medication and support. Depending on the substance and severity, detox may take place in an inpatient setting with 24-hour monitoring or, for milder cases, in a closely supervised outpatient setting. The goal is to keep you safe and comfortable and to prepare you for the next stage of treatment.

Why Detox Can Be Medically Necessary

For some substances, stopping abruptly without medical support can be dangerous. This is a major reason plans cover detox as a medical service rather than treating it as optional.

Alcohol

Alcohol withdrawal can be serious and, in severe cases, life-threatening. Supervised detox helps manage symptoms safely. See alcohol detox.

Opioids

Opioid withdrawal is intensely uncomfortable, and medication can ease it while reducing relapse risk. See opioid treatment.

Benzodiazepines

Benzodiazepine withdrawal can be dangerous and usually requires a carefully managed, gradual taper under medical supervision.

Other Substances

Withdrawal from other drugs may still warrant monitoring, especially when other health conditions are present.

How NYSHIP Detox Coverage Typically Works

Because detox is generally treated as medically necessary care, NYSHIP plans commonly cover it. A few things shape how your coverage applies:

  • Medical necessity: coverage typically requires that detox be clinically appropriate based on your symptoms and history.
  • Prior authorization: inpatient detox often must be approved in advance. We can help coordinate this with your plan.
  • In-network providers: using participating providers typically lowers your share of the cost.
  • Level of care: your plan covers the setting — inpatient or outpatient — that matches your clinical needs.

Parity law plays an important role here. Under the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA), most plans cannot apply harsher limits or higher costs to substance-use care, including detox, than they apply to comparable medical care.

What Detox Does and Does Not Do

Detox addresses the physical side of dependence, but on its own it is rarely enough for lasting recovery. That is why detox is usually the entry point to a broader plan that may include residential treatment, partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient care, or medication-assisted treatment. Coordinating coverage across these levels helps care continue smoothly as you step down.

Evidence-based behavioral therapies are an important part of what follows detox. Structured aftercare approaches — including cognitive-behavioral relapse prevention and mindfulness-based relapse prevention (MBRP) — help people build the skills needed to recognize high-risk situations and respond to cravings without returning to use. The federal Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act protects your access to these behavioral health services on terms comparable to medical care. Our team can explain how these aftercare options fit within your NYSHIP outpatient benefits when we verify your coverage.

Page last reviewed August 2026 by the NYSHIP Detox Editorial Team.

Understanding Your Costs

We do not quote specific dollar figures because they vary by plan and year. Your out-of-pocket cost for detox generally depends on your deductible, your copay or coinsurance, whether the provider is in-network, and your annual out-of-pocket maximum. We can walk you through these factors when we verify your benefits.

Verify Your Detox Benefits — Free and Confidential

If you think you or a loved one may need detox, you do not have to wait to understand your coverage. Our team can confirm what your NYSHIP or Empire Plan benefits include and help arrange any authorization — at no cost and with your privacy protected under 42 CFR Part 2 and HIPAA. Start with a free coverage verification. This page is informational and not medical advice; if you are in crisis, call or text 988, or reach the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357.

Call 631-800-4691 to find out what your plan covers for detox.

title: NYSHIP Residential Treatment & Inpatient Rehab
desc: How NYSHIP and the Empire Plan typically cover residential and inpatient rehab, when it is appropriate, and how authorization works. Call 631-800-4691.
h1: NYSHIP Coverage for Residential & Inpatient Rehab
bodyHtml:
Updated July 2026. NYSHIP and Empire Plan coverage for residential treatment remains in place for the 2026 plan year. Because benefit details and prior-authorization procedures can shift at annual enrollment, verify your current benefits before beginning care.

For some people, recovery begins best in a structured, round-the-clock setting. Residential treatment — sometimes called inpatient rehab — provides 24-hour clinical support away from the triggers of daily life. If you are a New York State or government employee, your NYSHIP coverage, most often the Empire Plan, typically covers residential treatment when it is medically necessary. Coverage varies by your specific plan, but this level of care is a recognized and commonly covered part of the treatment continuum.

What Is Residential Treatment?

Residential treatment is a live-in level of care where you stay at a facility and receive structured therapy, medical oversight, and peer support throughout the day. It sits above outpatient care in intensity and is designed for people who need more support and stability than they can get while living at home. Many programs combine individual and group therapy, relapse-prevention skills, and, when appropriate, medication management.

When Residential Care Is Appropriate

Clinicians often use the American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) criteria to match a person to the right level of care. Residential treatment may be appropriate when a lower level of care would not be safe or effective. Common factors include:

  • A higher severity of addiction or a long history of use.
  • Previous attempts at outpatient treatment that did not hold.
  • An unstable or unsupportive home environment.
  • Co-occurring mental-health conditions that benefit from close support, such as dual diagnosis care.
  • A need for continued monitoring after detox.

How NYSHIP Residential Coverage Typically Works

Medical Necessity

Coverage typically depends on a clinical assessment showing that residential care is the appropriate level for your needs.

Prior Authorization

Residential stays usually require pre-authorization. We help coordinate this with your plan so care is not delayed.

In-Network Providers

Using participating providers typically lowers your share of the cost and simplifies billing.

Concurrent Review

Plans often review progress during the stay to confirm continued medical necessity for ongoing days.

How Length of Stay Is Determined

There is no single fixed length that applies to everyone. The medically necessary length of stay is driven by clinical factors rather than a calendar, and your plan generally covers the days that are clinically justified. Factors that influence length of stay include the severity of the addiction, your response to treatment, the presence of co-occurring conditions, and the stability of your support system as you prepare to step down. As you progress, care often transitions to a less intensive setting such as partial hospitalization or intensive outpatient care.

Understanding Your Costs

We do not quote specific dollar amounts, because they vary by plan and year. Your out-of-pocket cost for residential care generally depends on your deductible, your copay or coinsurance, whether the facility is in-network, prior-authorization requirements, and your annual out-of-pocket maximum. We can explain how these apply to your situation during verification.

Parity law matters here too: under the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA), most plans cannot place harsher limits on residential addiction treatment than on comparable medical inpatient care.

Protecting Your Job and Privacy

Stepping away for residential treatment can feel daunting, but important legal protections exist for New York State employees. The Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) may provide eligible employees with up to 12 weeks of job-protected, unpaid leave per year for a serious health condition—a category that includes substance use disorder treatment. Many New York State employees may also have access to paid leave accruals, agency-specific leave policies, or union-negotiated protections that allow for a residential stay with less financial strain than FMLA alone. Your Employee Assistance Program (EAP) can often help coordinate leave paperwork and communicate with HR without disclosing the nature of your treatment.

Your privacy is equally protected. Federal law under 42 CFR Part 2—a regulation that imposes stricter confidentiality rules than standard HIPAA—means that substance use disorder treatment records cannot be shared with your employer, supervisor, or union without your explicit written consent. The fact that you sought residential treatment will not appear on standard employment records. Reaching out for help is medically and legally your right.

Verify Your Residential Benefits

If residential treatment may be the right step, we can confirm what your NYSHIP or Empire Plan covers and help arrange authorization — free and confidential. Start with a coverage verification. This page is informational and not medical advice; the right level of care should be determined with a qualified clinician.

Call 631-800-4691 to learn what your plan covers for residential rehab.

title: NYSHIP Outpatient Treatment | Empire Plan IOP & PHP Coverage
desc: NYSHIP outpatient treatment: how the Empire Plan covers PHP, IOP and evening or telehealth care around your job. Verify your benefits at 631-800-4691.
h1: NYSHIP Outpatient Treatment: Empire Plan Coverage for PHP, IOP and Care That Fits Around Your Job
bodyHtml:
Most people who need help with alcohol or drugs do not need to leave home for a month to get it. For a large share of New York State and local government employees, NYSHIP outpatient treatment is the level of care that makes recovery workable: structured, evidence-based programming several days a week, often in the evening or by secure video, while you keep your job, your paycheck and your routine. This page explains what outpatient treatment includes, how partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient and standard outpatient care differ, how the Empire Plan typically covers each, how prior authorization and copays generally work, and when outpatient is the right call versus when detox or residential care needs to come first. If you would rather ask a person, call 631-800-4691 for a confidential benefits check.

What Counts as NYSHIP Outpatient Treatment?

Outpatient means you live at home and travel to treatment, or log in to it, rather than staying overnight in a facility. Within that definition there is a wide range of intensity. Clinicians use the ASAM criteria, a national framework for matching people to levels of care, and the outpatient levels sit in the middle of it: more structure than a weekly therapy appointment, less than a hospital bed. The Empire Plan's Mental Health and Substance Use Program, administered by Carelon Behavioral Health (formerly Beacon Health Options), recognizes these levels and typically covers them when a clinical assessment shows they are medically necessary.

Outpatient programs generally combine group therapy, individual counseling, education about how substance use disorders work, relapse-prevention skills, family sessions and, where appropriate, coordination with medication-assisted treatment. Many also address co-occurring depression, anxiety, trauma or ADHD, since untreated mental health conditions are one of the most common reasons recovery stalls. Our NYSHIP mental health coverage page covers that side of the benefit.

PHP vs IOP vs Standard Outpatient

These three levels are often lumped together, but they differ in hours, intensity and who they suit.

Partial hospitalization (PHP)

PHP is the most intensive outpatient level. Programs generally run five or six hours a day, five days a week, during the daytime. You go home each evening. PHP is common as a step down from detox or residential care, and as a starting point for people who need close to full-time structure but have a stable, substance-free place to sleep. Because it occupies the workday, PHP usually requires time off, and FMLA or accrued leave typically covers it.

Intensive outpatient (IOP)

IOP is the level most working people use. Programs generally meet three to five days a week for about three hours per session, and many run in the evening specifically so participants can keep working. A typical IOP lasts eight to twelve weeks, though length is driven by progress rather than the calendar. IOP is appropriate for people who are medically stable, motivated, and able to stay away from alcohol and drugs between sessions with the support the program provides.

Standard outpatient

Standard outpatient care is one to three hours a week: individual therapy, a weekly group, medication management visits, or a combination. It is where most people land after IOP, and it can continue for a year or longer. For some people with milder or early-stage problems and strong supports, it is also a reasonable place to start.

A quick way to think about the three: PHP is a full-time job you go home from, IOP is a demanding part-time commitment that fits around a full-time job, and standard outpatient is ongoing maintenance. Most people move down the ladder over time, and some move back up temporarily if things get shaky. Our levels of addiction care page places all of these alongside detox and residential treatment.

Evening and Telehealth Scheduling Around a State Job

The single biggest obstacle to outpatient treatment for public employees is the calendar, and programs have adapted. Two developments matter most.

Evening IOP. Many intensive outpatient programs now hold sessions that begin in the late afternoon or early evening and end by mid-evening. A teacher can attend after dismissal; a state office worker can go after a standard shift; a corrections officer or nurse on rotating shifts can often find a program with more than one time slot. Weekend and early-morning options exist in some areas as well.

Telehealth. Secure video has made IOP and standard outpatient care available from home, and for many NYSHIP members that is the difference between finishing a program and dropping out in week three. Telehealth removes the commute, the parking, the childcare problem and the risk of running into someone in a waiting room. It is typically covered by the Empire Plan on the same terms as in-person care for outpatient levels, though this varies by plan and provider. Our telehealth addiction treatment page covers the details. Detox and residential care, by their nature, cannot be delivered virtually.

When you call, tell us your actual schedule, including shift rotations, commute times and any dates you cannot miss. Matching the program to the life you have is most of the work.

What the Empire Plan Typically Covers for Outpatient Care

Under the federal Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act, plans that cover substance use treatment generally cannot impose stricter limits on it than on comparable medical care. For Empire Plan members that typically means:

  • Partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient and standard outpatient substance use treatment are covered levels of care when medically necessary.
  • Individual, group and family therapy delivered as part of outpatient treatment are typically covered.
  • Medication management visits and MAT medications such as buprenorphine, naltrexone and acamprosate are typically covered under the behavioral health, medical or pharmacy benefit as appropriate.
  • In-network outpatient care in many cases involves a per-visit copay rather than a deductible, while out-of-network care is reimbursed at a lower rate and leaves you responsible for more.
  • Telehealth for outpatient behavioral health is typically covered on comparable terms to in-person care.

Every one of those statements carries the same caveat: coverage varies by plan, and verifying your own benefits is the only way to know your numbers. We never quote dollar figures on this site because they change by plan year and by plan, but we will give you yours during verification.

How Prior Authorization and Copays Generally Work

Two mechanics cause most of the confusion around NYSHIP outpatient treatment, so they are worth explaining in general terms.

Prior authorization. Some services must be approved by the plan's behavioral health program before they begin for benefits to apply. Inpatient and residential care almost always require it. PHP and IOP frequently do, depending on the plan and provider. Standard outpatient visits often do not require authorization in advance, though the plan may review ongoing care periodically. In practice, the treatment program handles the request: a clinician submits an assessment showing why the level of care is appropriate, and the plan certifies a number of days or sessions, with continued-stay reviews as treatment progresses. You should not have to argue your own case. Our NYSHIP prior authorization guide explains the process and what to do if a request is denied.

Copays, deductibles and out-of-pocket maximums. For in-network outpatient behavioral health, many Empire Plan members pay a fixed copay per visit or per program day, and nothing more. Out-of-network care typically runs through a deductible and coinsurance instead, with the member responsible for any amount above what the plan considers reasonable. An annual out-of-pocket maximum caps what you spend on covered in-network care in a year. Where you fall depends on your plan and whether you choose a network provider. Our page on NYSHIP copays and deductibles for rehab goes deeper, and a benefits check gives you the actual figures.

When Outpatient Is Appropriate and When It Is Not

Outpatient care is the right starting point for many people, but not for everyone, and pretending otherwise is dangerous. In general, outpatient treatment is a good fit when:

  • You are not physically dependent on alcohol or benzodiazepines in a way that makes withdrawal medically risky, or you have already completed detox.
  • You have a stable place to live where alcohol and drugs are not constantly present.
  • You are motivated to attend and can get to sessions, in person or by video, reliably.
  • Any co-occurring mental health condition is stable enough to be managed alongside treatment.
  • Previous outpatient attempts, if any, did not end in quick relapse.

Detox needs to come first when you drink heavily every day or take benzodiazepines regularly, because withdrawal from either can cause seizures and can be fatal without medical management. Opioid detox is rarely dangerous but is far more tolerable with medical support, and it is often where buprenorphine is started. Our NYSHIP detox coverage page explains that level.

Residential or inpatient care is usually recommended when someone has relapsed repeatedly after outpatient treatment, has overdosed, lives in an environment saturated with use, has a serious co-occurring psychiatric condition, or simply cannot stop while living at home. It is not a failure to need it, and outpatient care is nearly always the step down afterward. See NYSHIP residential treatment for how that benefit typically works. A clinical assessment, not a website, makes this determination, and we will not talk you into a lower level of care than you need.

Outpatient Options for Long Island, New York City and Capital Region Commuters

NYSHIP members are spread across the state, and the outpatient question looks a little different in each region.

Long Island. Nassau and Suffolk have evening IOP options, and the sheer amount of time Long Islanders spend commuting makes telehealth especially attractive. For state employees at Stony Brook, Farmingdale State, Pilgrim, DOT Region 10 or the courts, and for school district and municipal employees on NYSHIP, our NYSHIP rehab on Long Island page covers the local picture in depth.

New York City. State employees in the five boroughs have the widest selection of outpatient programs anywhere in the state and a transit system that makes evening attendance realistic from most neighborhoods. See NYSHIP rehab in New York City.

The Capital Region. For the large state workforce in and around Albany, outpatient care raises particular privacy concerns because so many people work for the same employer. Telehealth and programs a short drive from the office both help. Our NYSHIP rehab in Albany page has more.

Wherever you are, the Empire Plan benefit itself does not change by region; what changes is which programs are convenient, and we help sort that out.

What a Typical Week in IOP Looks Like

To make this concrete, here is a general picture of an evening IOP week. Programs differ, but the shape is common.

  • Three or four evenings of roughly three hours each, starting after the workday. Each session usually opens with a check-in, moves into a skills or education topic, and ends with process group where members talk about what actually happened that week.
  • One individual session with your counselor, in person or by video, to work on your own plan.
  • Medication visits as needed, for MAT or for co-occurring conditions.
  • A family session every week or two, often in the evening, for people whose family is involved.
  • Drug and alcohol testing on a regular or random basis, which most participants come to see as helpful accountability rather than surveillance.
  • Homework between sessions: tracking triggers, practicing skills, attending a mutual-support meeting.

As you progress, sessions typically taper to two evenings, then one, and then you move to standard outpatient care. Many programs also offer alumni groups that continue indefinitely.

Leave and Job Protection for Appointments

Evening IOP and telehealth mean that many people complete NYSHIP outpatient treatment without taking any leave at all. When schedules do collide, the federal Family and Medical Leave Act allows eligible employees to take leave intermittently, in blocks as small as a few hours, for treatment of a serious health condition, and substance use disorder treatment qualifies when a health care provider delivers or refers you to it. Accrued sick leave often covers PHP-level days off, and some bargaining agreements add protections. Your treatment records remain protected under 42 CFR Part 2 and HIPAA throughout. Our guides to FMLA and rehab for NY state employees and confidentiality for state employees cover the specifics.

Verify Your NYSHIP Benefits

If PHP or IOP sounds like it fits, the next step is a short, confidential benefits check. Call 631-800-4691 any time, or email support@alumniaidservices.com, and we will confirm your Empire Plan outpatient coverage, network options, copays and any authorization requirements, then help you find a schedule that works. You can also begin with our coverage verification page. This page is informational and not medical advice; the right level of care should be decided with a qualified clinician. If you or someone you love is in immediate danger, call or text 988, or reach the free SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357.

faq.a: Often, yes. Many IOPs hold evening sessions specifically for working adults, and telehealth IOP and outpatient counseling are widely available. The Empire Plan typically covers telehealth for outpatient behavioral health on terms comparable to in-person care, though this varies by plan and provider. Detox and residential care cannot be delivered virtually.

faq.q: Does outpatient treatment need prior authorization under the Empire Plan?
faq.a: It depends on the level. PHP and IOP frequently require certification through the plan's behavioral health program before benefits apply; standard outpatient visits often do not, though ongoing care may be reviewed periodically. The treatment program normally submits the request on your behalf, and we help coordinate it.

faq.q: How much does NYSHIP outpatient treatment cost?
faq.a: It depends on your plan and whether the provider is in network. In many cases in-network outpatient behavioral health involves a fixed copay per visit or program day; out-of-network care usually runs through a deductible and coinsurance. We do not publish dollar figures because they vary by plan year, but a benefits check gives you your actual numbers.

faq.q: How do I know whether I need outpatient care or detox and residential treatment?
faq.a: A clinical assessment decides this. Detox comes first if you drink heavily every day or take benzodiazepines regularly, because withdrawal from either can be dangerous. Residential care is usually recommended after repeated relapse, an overdose, an unsafe home environment or a serious co-occurring condition. Otherwise outpatient is frequently an appropriate starting point.

faq.q: Will my employer find out I am in an outpatient program?
faq.a: Not through your insurance. Claims go to the Empire Plan's behavioral health program, and your records are protected by 42 CFR Part 2 and HIPAA. Evening and telehealth schedules mean many people need no leave at all; if you do use FMLA, the certification your employer sees is limited in what it must include.

faq.q: How do I verify my NYSHIP outpatient benefits?
faq.a: Call 631-800-4691 with your Empire Plan or NYSHIP card. We contact the plan's Mental Health and Substance Use Program, confirm your PHP, IOP and outpatient coverage, and explain copays, network options and authorization in plain language. The check is free, confidential and does not commit you to anything.

title: Free NYSHIP Rehab Coverage Verification
desc: Verify your NYSHIP or Empire Plan rehab benefits free and confidentially. See what we check and what you need to get started. Call 631-800-4691.
h1: Verify Your NYSHIP Rehab Benefits — Free & Confidential
bodyHtml:
Updated July 2026. NYSHIP and Empire Plan benefit verification procedures described here reflect the 2026 plan year. Coverage details can change at annual open enrollment, so always confirm your current benefits before starting treatment.

Understanding your benefits should not be a barrier to getting help. If you are a New York State or government employee, our team can verify your NYSHIP or Empire Plan addiction-treatment benefits quickly, at no cost, and with your privacy fully protected. This page explains how verification works, what information you will need, and what we check on your behalf.

Why Verify Your Benefits First?

Benefits vary from plan to plan and from year to year, and the rules around authorization and networks can be hard to interpret on your own. Verifying first removes the guesswork: you learn what your plan typically covers, what your likely responsibilities are, and what steps come next — before any decisions are made. It is one of the simplest ways to reduce stress and avoid surprises at a difficult time.

What You Will Need

To verify your benefits, it helps to have a few details ready. Do not worry if you are missing something — we can often work with what you have.

  • Insurance information: the member ID and group number from your NYSHIP or Empire Plan card.
  • Policyholder details: the name and date of birth of the covered employee or dependent seeking care.
  • A general sense of needs: the substance involved and any urgent concerns, so we can point you toward the right level of care.

You do not need to have everything figured out. Part of our job is to help you make sense of it.

What We Check for You

Covered Levels of Care

We confirm what your plan typically covers, from detox to residential to PHP and IOP and medication-assisted treatment.

Authorization Rules

We identify which services may need prior authorization and help coordinate it so care is not delayed.

Network Status

We review in-network options, since using participating providers typically lowers your share of the cost.

Cost Factors

We explain the deductible, copay or coinsurance, and out-of-pocket factors that shape what you may owe.

MAT & Medication Coverage

We confirm whether medications for opioid or alcohol use disorder, such as buprenorphine or naltrexone, are covered under your medical or pharmacy benefit.

How the Process Works

Verification is straightforward and usually fast:

  • Reach out. Call or email and share your basic insurance details.
  • We review. Our team checks your NYSHIP or Empire Plan benefits and any authorization requirements.
  • We explain. You get a clear, plain-language summary of what is typically covered and what to expect.
  • You decide. There is no obligation. If you choose to move forward, we help coordinate next steps.

Free, Confidential, and Protected by Law

Verification is always free, and your privacy is protected throughout. Federal rules under 42 CFR Part 2 and HIPAA safeguard the confidentiality of substance-use treatment information, with strict limits on when it can be shared. Reaching out for a benefits check does not obligate you to anything, and it will not appear to anyone you have not authorized.

A Word on Parity and Your Rights

The Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA) requires most plans to cover addiction treatment on terms no more restrictive than medical care. Regulations strengthening MHPAEA that took effect for recent plan years require insurers to document that any non-quantitative treatment limitations — such as prior authorization, step therapy, or network adequacy rules applied to behavioral health — are no more restrictive than those applied to medical benefits. If your claim is denied, you have the right to request a written explanation of the basis for any treatment limitation applied to your addiction care. Knowing this can help you advocate effectively for the coverage you are entitled to. Eligible employees may also have job protection through the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) while in treatment — ask about FMLA when you call.

Ready to Verify Your Coverage?

Whether you are exploring options for yourself or a loved one, a free verification is a low-pressure first step. To learn more about what your plan may include, see our rehab coverage overview or Empire Plan coverage details. This page is informational and not medical advice. If you are in crisis, call or text 988, or reach the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357 for free, confidential, 24/7 support.

Call 631-800-4691 or email support@alumniaidservices.com to start your free, confidential verification.

faq.q: Is the coverage verification really free?
faq.a: Yes. Verifying your NYSHIP or Empire Plan benefits is completely free and carries no obligation. You can learn what your plan covers before making any decisions.

faq.q: Is the verification confidential?
faq.a: Yes. Your information is protected under federal rules including 42 CFR Part 2 and HIPAA, which safeguard the confidentiality of substance-use treatment information.

faq.q: What information do I need to verify benefits?
faq.a: It helps to have your member ID and group number, the policyholder's name and date of birth, and a general sense of the care needed. If you are missing details, we can often work with what you have.

faq.q: What do you check during verification?
faq.a: We confirm the levels of care your plan typically covers, identify any prior-authorization requirements, review in-network options, and explain the cost factors that may apply to you.

faq.q: Am I obligated to enter treatment if I verify?
faq.a: No. Verification is informational and carries no obligation. If you choose to move forward, we help coordinate next steps, but the decision is always yours.

faq.q: How long does verification take?
faq.a: It is usually fast. After you share your basic insurance details, our team reviews your benefits and gives you a clear, plain-language summary of what to expect.

faq.q: How do I start a verification?
faq.a: Call 631-800-4691 or email support@alumniaidservices.com. We will review your NYSHIP or Empire Plan coverage and explain your options at no cost.
